evidence: Two Yellows: the distinctive five-by-five square grid has the same alternating pale/deep yellow half-cell pattern, including undivided darker second and fourth columns. The 1952 Marks work lies within the 1948–1954 scope of the Foundation-captioned exhibition. Full square support and unequal yellow field boundaries agree. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 52. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

Two Blacks, White and Blue: the primary Philadelphia Museum of Art exhibition page explicitly identifies EK 70 as the 1955 oil-on-canvas work, four joined panels, 92 × 24 in (233.7 × 61 cm). The historical Guggenheim entry has the exact title, date, dimensions and distinctive vertical sequence of black square, white band, black square and blue lower rectangle. This is an exact identifier plus material/dimension bridge. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 70. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

Jersey: identical distinctive green-and-white landscape painting with a broad green diagonal curved strip, white wedge at upper right, and narrow white diagonal passage at lower left. The 1958 historical object and 1996 retrospective installation agree in uncommon field geometry and support proportions; this is more specific than a plain green panel. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 169. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

Red Curve IV: identical red segment inside the lower-right white half-square, with matching diagonal chord, convex arc, white triangular backing and pointed endpoints. The primary Grenoble object dates the work 1973 and gives 254 × 254 cm; the 1988 Foundation-captioned installation depicts that specific half-square composition. The painted white lower/right support is retained. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 491. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

Diagonal with Curve III: identical narrow black ascending diagonal band with a curved left edge and short vertical cuts at both ends. The 1978 Philadelphia painting in the primary 1996 essay figure 3 has that distinctive contour and portrait outer aspect, and was shown in the 1963–1979 retrospective documented by the Foundation. No unrelated numbered diagonal curve was substituted. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 564. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

Charter: identical two-part composition with an unevenly rounded orange quadrilateral on a white upper ground above a black rectangular lower panel; the outline and the upper/lower division match the specifically captioned Yale 1959 photograph. The primary Foundation text identifies Charter among the eight paintings selected for Sixteen Americans in 1959, matching the museum date and distinctive motif. Physical dimensions remain unknown. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 226. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

Blue over Blue / Blue on Blue: identical unusual blue rectangular backing and raised curved D-shaped overlay, with the same slight left projection and long right convex edge. Foundation chronology names Blue over Blue in the 1964 Post-Painterly Abstraction exhibition, independently cited in the current LACMA object bibliography for Blue on Blue 1963. The 1973 Foundation photograph matches the actual current LACMA image. A differing historical 1973 height report remains unresolved; current LACMA 203.2 × 152.4 × 19.05 cm and its explicit Paintings classification remain unchanged. This museum-classified painted-aluminum relief is not excluded as a sculpture. Foundation image caption explicitly supplies EK 317. Both actual photographs were visually inspected; colour names alone did not establish identity.

The Foundation 1951 installation explicitly labels Ormesson EK 29 and shows all three joined panels: the black left stripe and green inverted-U motif in the first panel, bent green vertical stripe in the centre, and black upper-left frame/green verticals in the third. These exact distinctive motifs agree with the colour triptych reproduced as Ormesson 1950 in the university thesis figure 25, printed page 65. The primary Foundation chronology names the work in the 1951 exhibition, and the 1973 MoMA catalogue note 26 calls Ormesson a 1950 painting. Secondary thesis dimensions are not silently promoted to primary physical-scale facts.
